title: Barabbas and the Crowd's Choice
reflectionText: Barabbas was guilty, and that morning he walked free. Jesus was innocent, and he was led away to the cross in his place. The one man who most deserved that cross was the one man who did not go to it. Barabbas never spoke a word; he was simply let go.
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-07-24, Batch D (gap CG09). Matthew 27:15-26, the Barabbas choice, absent both lanes. SHORT only, WEB 302w / KJV 301w. Owner directive observed: Matthew 27:25 ('His blood be on us and on our children') is included exactly and faithfully AS THE CROWD'S CRY, with NO added commentary assigning the action to Jewish people generally, to later generations, or to anyone beyond the participants the passage names. The text's own attribution is kept intact: 'the chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes' (27:20). The reflection deliberately centers Barabbas and the substitution (the guilty freed, the innocent led away in his place), not collective guilt. Ends on 27:26 (Barabbas released, Jesus scourged and delivered to be crucified). Narrator/mood/length were authoring selections (title/anchor owner-given) — flagged for owner review.
